3.0 Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment

3.1 HAZARD IDENTIFICATION METHODS:

☐ Job Safety Analysis (JSA) - All critical tasks

☐ Workplace Inspections - Daily, Weekly, Monthly

☐ Safety Observations - Continuous

☐ Incident Investigation - All incidents

☐ Hazard Reporting System - Employee reporting

☐ Pre-task Planning - Before each job

3.2 RISK ASSESSMENT MATRIX:

INSIGNIFICANTMINORMODERATEMAJORCATASTROPHIC
RARE1 (LOW)2 (LOW)3 (MEDIUM)4 (MEDIUM)5 (HIGH)
UNLIKELY2 (LOW)4 (MEDIUM)6 (MEDIUM)8 (HIGH)10 (HIGH)
POSSIBLE3 (MEDIUM)6 (MEDIUM)9 (HIGH)12 (HIGH)15 (CRITICAL)
LIKELY4 (MEDIUM)8 (HIGH)12 (HIGH)16 (CRITICAL)20 (CRITICAL)
ALMOST CERTAIN5 (HIGH)10 (HIGH)15 (CRITICAL)20 (CRITICAL)25 (CRITICAL)

RISK RATING: LOW (1-4) = Accept; MEDIUM (5-9) = Manage; HIGH (10-15) = Urgent Action; CRITICAL (16-25) = Stop

4.0 Operational Controls

4.1 HIERARCHY OF CONTROLS:

☐ ELIMINATION - Remove the hazard completely

☐ SUBSTITUTION - Replace with less hazardous alternative

☐ ENGINEERING CONTROLS - Guarding, ventilation, isolation

☐ ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROLS - Procedures, training, signs

☐ PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT - Last line of defense

7.0 Incident Investigation & Corrective Action

7.1 INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION:

☐ FATALITY - Immediate notification to senior management, regulatory authorities

☐ SERIOUS INJURY - Investigation within 24 hours, root cause analysis

☐ LOST TIME - Investigation within 48 hours, corrective action plan

☐ MEDICAL TREATMENT - Investigation within 1 week

☐ FIRST AID - Investigation as appropriate

☐ NEAR MISS - Investigation to prevent recurrence

7.2 INVESTIGATION PROCESS:

STEP 1: Secure the scene

STEP 2: Notify appropriate personnel

STEP 3: Gather evidence (photos, documents, interviews)

STEP 4: Conduct root cause analysis (5 Whys, Fishbone)

STEP 5: Develop corrective actions

STEP 6: Implement and track actions

STEP 7: Share lessons learned
